beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output.
beats.got: Nobody promises me safe, only a check I keep running. That's more honest than I expected.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** residual risk: what is left, and what future sessions need before touching the system
beats.got: nothing new. It's a verb list of the kind I've seen on every programme slide.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I'm asked to think of my own checks before being told any. Fair.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent's 'action' is just text a harness turns into a real operation, so a vague description or poisoned context goes straight through.

beats.trigger: Agent systems do not offer certainty.
beats.got: The course admits it can't make this safe. Not the usual pitch.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: Old security assumed repeatable behaviour. Fine, I knew that.

beats.trigger: The dangerous move is getting your agent to *decide* to do something harmful with access it has, through well-formed English in a document it reads.
beats.got: An ordinary document can steer the agent into misusing what it already has access to. That is new, and it's not in my last three transformations.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: Five concrete levers. Sounds like a framework, but at least the items are usable.

beats.trigger: **"I can't tell"** is a real answer. Closing it takes evidence, not a better guess.
beats.got: Writing down what's left and signing for it. That's sensible risk management, and 'I can't tell' is permitted.

beats.trigger: Scope it down far enough and the system is safe and useless.
beats.got: Safety and usefulness trade off, and the course says so plainly.

beats.trigger: Expect it to cost you a feature.
beats.got: The best control is not connecting the thing at all, and that costs something. Straight talk.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: The author admits it's complex. I like that more than a confident slogan, though the closing line is a bit of a poster.

beats.trigger: A **skill** packages an expertise (rules, checklists, the moves an agent runs) into something the agent loads when the work matches.
beats.got: A skill is a saved, reusable check. Like a checklist the agent can load. OK.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: Run against our own policies, the agent sorts rules into checkable and not checkable. That's something I can test myself.

beats.trigger: Push back on anything that sounds like a generic GDPR brochure.
beats.got: I tell it what matters in my company, and it should not hand me boilerplate. I'd test that.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: Twenty-two minutes of Q&A to build the check. Plausibly useful, long though.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: When I don't know, I hand the decision back. Slightly too neat, but practical.

beats.trigger: The save mechanic differs by runtime.
beats.got: Installation steps for different tools. Admin.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: This doesn't replace our existing security controls. Good, because legal would ask.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: The aim is a repeatable loop, not a pass mark.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The check finds gaps I hadn't thought of and admits where it can't judge. I can verify that myself.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: Ranked agent risks I can interrogate. The 'feeling is evidence' line is a touch precious.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: I apply one fix, re-run the check, and write down what's left. That's a real audit trail.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report.
beats.got: When the agent can't tell, I take a narrow question to legal or security. Sensible, and I'd do it anyway.

beats.trigger: We did this for one risk.
beats.got: We fixed one risk out of many, so what we built is still a prototype. Candid.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: The check is reusable on the next agent. 'Expert in the room' is overselling a bit.

beats.trigger: "That residual is too vague, name the file or behaviour."
beats.got: The agent adds rules to the instructions file from what happened, and I'm told to push back when it's vague.

beats.trigger: A skill is not a deployed service and does not settle ownership.
beats.got: Skills can be handed to a colleague. The limits are stated, which is fair.

beats.trigger: Well-formed English is the attack surface, even via sources.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors. Your call.
beats.got: Homework. I have a calendar full of steering groups.

beats.trigger: What check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two real cases of AI output going out unchecked: a lawyer and a consultancy report. Concrete, I may read them.

take_homes: An agent can be steered by ordinary text in a document it reads, so safety can't be judged from its output. You need a repeatable check.
The cheapest control is not opening the door (no write access, no mailbox), and it costs a feature. What remains gets written down and signed.
'I can't tell' is a legitimate verdict, and the next step is a narrow question to legal or security.

monday.move: Ask whoever runs our one pilot AI tool what it can read and write, and nothing else for now. Run the policy files against it only if that answer is vague.
monday.when: Sometime next week, if the steering group doesn't eat the slot
monday.stop_condition: I get a clear list of what it can reach, or it turns out nobody knows, which is the finding
monday.blocker: Calendar, and my scepticism about whether anything beyond the access question is worth my time

misconception.why: The prompt-injection-via-documents point and the admission that certainty isn't on offer didn't sound like agile or OKRs. It's not changed, though: I haven't seen this run on our systems, and this module is about caution, not about what the agents can do.

one_line: Surprisingly honest for a training. It tells you what it can't promise and gives you a check you can run yourself, but the 'discipline is what carries' parts still sound like a programme.
